title.narrative: Multi-sectoral Emergency Response in Ebenat Woreda

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe Amhara region is currently facing a new wave of conflict, following the Tigray conflict that had devastating effects on the region. The ongoing clashes between unidentified armed groups and the national government in the Amhara region, including in the Ebenat Woreda, are causing significant loss of lives and disruption of livelihoods for the local communities. The South Gondar Zone Disaster Risk Management Office reports that Ebenat is currently hosting around 1,800 internally displaced persons (IDPs), with a majority of them being women. These displaced individuals, who are living alongside the host communities, are experiencing extremely difficult conditions. The Zonal Disaster Risk Management department has highlighted issues such as malnutrition among children and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), lack of clean water supply, disease outbreaks, and shortages of both food and non-food items as direct consequences of the conflict.ltbrgtThe project's objective is to respond to unmet needs of internally displaced people in Ebenat Woreda, Amhara Region through an integrated and multi-sectoral approach. FH will use multi sectoral project interventions to deliver emergency WASH, health, and cash assistance for rental support to IDPs and people with disability in the Woreda, in collaboration with relevant clusters and local government authorities. In the health sector, FH will support the cluster's goal on health by ensuring that all individuals in need, including IDPs and the host community, have equitable access to vital life-saving health interventions through existing government run health institutions. Regarding WASH, FH will align with the WASH cluster's objectives by working to improve crucial sanitation and hygiene behavior changes, supporting life-saving and life-sustaining emergency and sustainable water supply solutions, as well as improving sanitation access for IDPs and host communities. Additionally, FH will assist IDPs and host communities through interventions under the emergency shelter and non-food items sector by providing essential items such as blankets, mattresses, etc as well as cash support. Cash will provide the target IDPs and people with disabiled community members with the purchasing power to access their basic rental needs and shelter as they see fit in a flexible and dignified manner. The allocated sum will be transferred to the recipients' bank accounts in accordance with the recommendations of Ethiopia's Cash Working Group (CWG).ltbrgtThe total budget allocated for the response is $600,000.ltbrgtlt/pgt
